points.en: Christian ethics is the disciplined study of how God's people are to live.
It is judged by the standard of God's own character as revealed in His Word, so it begins with God, not with human feelings, results or majority opinion.
The standard is already given; ethics is learning to live inside it rather than searching for one.
Discernment is not automatic; Scripture itself assumes believers must grow in it, so loving God and reading the Bible do not make ethical judgment automatic.
Ethical maturity is trained by use and practice, like senses exercised to tell good from evil, not given at conversion.
Paul prays that love abound in knowledge and discernment, and Hebrews rebukes those still on milk.
The goal of Christian ethics is the glory of God: everything is done to display His character and honor Him.
The world studies ethics to make society function, restrain harm or be happy, which are not bad but are not the goal.
A holy God is worthy of a holy people; ethics is worship with our hands and feet.
Scripture is God-breathed, and that gives it God's own authority over how we live.
It is useful for teaching truth, reproving wrong, correcting and training in righteousness.
Its sufficiency: the man of God is complete and thoroughly equipped for every good work, so the Word forms us as well as saves us.
Sufficiency does not mean Scripture gives a direct verse or command for every situation.
It means Scripture supplies everything needed (truth about God, ourselves, right and wrong, a renewed mind) to discern how to honor God in any situation.
Example: no verse says which job to take or which treatment to choose; the Bible is a foundation for reasoning, not a card catalog.
Secular systems place the moral standard in the creature or creation (consequences, reason, self, or nothing) rather than in God.
This fails because a standard resting on the creature can be no more stable, holy or authoritative than the creature, leaving preference dressed as principle.
These views see some truth (actions have results, human judgment is fallible), but err in where they rest their weight.
Relativism cannot be lived because the relativist appeals to justice the moment he is wronged, though he denies objective right and wrong.
Romans 2:15: the law is written on every heart because people are made in God's image, so everyone knows moral truth in conscience.
This is the pastor's point of contact, calling people back to a law they already know and suppress.
James 3:1: those who teach will receive a stricter judgment, so a pastor is held to a higher account.
A teacher of how to live carries a burden ordinary believers do not and is judged as a teacher; God does not grade on a curve.
This should sober the pastor each time he opens the Bible to instruct someone.
A pastor leads by his character and example, not only by his words (1 Peter 5:3; 1 Corinthians 11:1).
One can preach a sermon not lived but cannot pastor people one is not; where words and character contradict, character wins.
The congregation absorbs the shepherd's life, such as how he treats his wife and opponents, more than his sermons.
Ephesians 2:10: we are saved by grace, not by works, but created in Christ for good works prepared beforehand.
The order is grace first, then the holy life grace produces; works are the fruit, never the price, of salvation.
Why it matters: keep the order and ethics is joyful walking worthy of the One who bought us; reverse it and ethics becomes a law that crushes.
